APPLE BEGINS TESTING CXMT DRAM CHIPS FOR DEVICES SOLD IN CHINA — FT



$AAPL is exploring China’s CXMT for memory chips, boosting the state-backed chipmaker’s profile.

•	Apple has begun testing CXMT’s DRAM chips for devices sold in China.

•	Apple is leading a lobbying effort among U.S. tech companies to get broader use of CXMT’s products approved.

•	CXMT spent nearly a decade burning through billions before this turnaround.

•	Its net profit hit RMB 33 billion (about $4.8 billion) in Q1 2026, reversing RMB 37 billion (about $5.4 billion) in accumulated losses over the past decade.

•	CXMT is now central to Beijing’s push for a self-sufficient domestic AI supply chain.

*NVIDIA AND AI CHIP STARTUP D-MATRIX ARE COMBINING HARDWARE IN A NEW SYSTEM TO POWER AI MODELS - THE INFORMATION



Nvidia partners with AI chip rivals like d-Matrix to combine hardware. Strategy helps Nvidia adapt to competition and generate new revenue.

Samsung has begun mass production of its most advanced data center storage drive, which is set for use inside Nvidia Corp.’s upcoming Vera Rubin platform.



The product — the PM1763 enterprise solid-state drive — was unveiled at Nvidia’s GTC conference earlier this year. Samsung showcased it alongside its next-generation high-bandwidth memory, or HBM4, and low-power SOCAMM2 module as part of a comprehensive package designed for AI data centers.

•	The PM1763 is a PCIe 6.0-based enterprise SSD optimized for AI and HPC servers.

•	It uses Samsung’s 9th-generation V-NAND and a new 4-nanometer controller.

•	It’s available in 4TB, 8TB, and 16TB capacities.
